entry-web.description: Where the browser starts: the router, the document with its Splash for iOS, the offline page, and one thin route for each Place. The router reaches the routes through the generated route tree, so nothing imports them

entry-worker.description: Where the Worker starts: /rpc goes to the Ledger API, everything else to the app

entry-infra.description: Deployable resources, composed by alchemy.run.ts: the D1 database, its table, and the Worker

client-screens.description: What the user sees: the shell around every Place, each Place, the sheets over them, and the parts they share

client-commands.description: The vocabulary: every Command with its keys, the gesture that gives it on a touch screen, the guide to every gesture, and how each sounds and shows when given

client-state.description: What the browser keeps and when: the app machine that finds who is signed in and holds one User's Session open, that Session with the User's money in step with D1, this device's Settings, and the copies of every signed-in User

app-state.description: The app machine opens and closes Sessions and keeps the copies; screens read the open Session and the device's Settings

client-kit.description: What Ledger needed that no package has yet: sounds made on demand, the Thumb Lock, the Place Picker with its Lift Hint, and what the device can be driven by. Each knows nothing of Ledger

server.description: The Worker's side: the D1 table of every User's money, the Ledger API's handlers, and the host that answers /rpc for the User who signed the request

domain.description: The words of money, Accounts, Categories, Entries and the currency, with the sums over them and the Ledger API both sides speak; and the device's Settings

kstack.description: Read top-down as the folders: entry starts the browser and the Worker; the client's screens over its commands and state; the server; the domain both sides speak at the bottom
